- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and overpredicts continuation — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is mixed or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.30), model frequently underestimates upward momentum — increase forecast by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the first 5–7 days of a new trend — apply a 3–5% upward bias to early forecast days if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative and price is trending upward, model often fails to recognize the reversal — reduce forecast slope to reflect diminishing momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative but price is rising, model tends to over-predict the rise — cap forecast increase at 3–5% above prior peak to avoid over-optimism.  
- Model often underestimates true price in the final 5–7 days of a 30-day forecast — apply a 2–4% upward bias to end of forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
